findings.title: R does nothing on the result card or the Lunch fail card, though both buttons show an R keycap
findings.problem: The result card's 'Play again' button (src/ui/screens.ts:198) and the Lunch fail card's 'Retry' button (src/ui/screens.ts:225) both carry an 'R' keycap badge, but pressing R on either card does nothing. The game's R handler restarts only when `playing = this.running && !this.won` (src/game.ts:166). Both end states set `won=true`: win() at src/game.ts:350, and the Lunch fail at src/lunch-runtime.ts:285, where `g.won=true` is set on failure. GameUI.key (src/ui/game-ui.ts:119) only calls flagAutostart() for the result and fail screens and never reloads. I measured it: on the Playground result card, R left the screen on 'result' 2.5 s later. On the Lunch spoil card, R left the screen on 'fail' 3 s later. Both times sessionStorage was left holding a stale autostart flag. Only Enter or a click retries. A player who believes the keycap presses R, nothing happens, and they think the game has hung. That breaks DR-19 (the key does what the prompt says) and DR-20 (a cheap one-key retry), right when the player has just failed. This looks like a side effect of the L6 fix (65a7344), which limited R to 'during play'.
findings.fix: In GameUI.key (src/ui/game-ui.ts:117-129), add: `else if((s==='result'||s==='fail')&&e.code==='KeyR'){e.preventDefault();this.restart();}`. restart() already calls flagAutostart and reloads. Alternatively, in game.ts:166 change the KeyR condition to `this.running` and let `won` through only when document.body.dataset.screen is 'result' or 'fail'. Keep the existing behaviour where R is ignored during the 1.4 s win push-in and the 1.2 s fail hold, so a stray press can't skip the payoff.
findings.verify: Add a test to tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts 'an unpowered fridge eventually spoils lunch and offers a retry': after the fail card shows, press R and expect body[data-screen=play] with job.failed false within 3 s. Add the same check after the Playground win in tests/routes.spec.ts. Re-run mockups/review5/tools/meta-settings-errors/flows.mjs and expect screen 'play' after R.
findings.verify_reason: Code: game.ts:166 restarts on KeyR only when `playing=this.running&&!this.won`. win() sets won=true (game.ts:350) and so does the Lunch fail (lunch-runtime.ts:285). GameUI.key:119 only calls flagAutostart for result/fail and never reloads. Reproduced: after a Playground win, R left the screen on 'result' 2.5 s later and sessionStorage held the stale autostart 'playground'. The R keycap is visible on the Play-again button in my shot. The pad's A button does reload on a won state (game.ts:189), so only keyboard players are affected. Not P0, because Enter and a click still work. The fix is right: restart() at game-ui.ts:74 does flagAutostart plus reload, and location.reload keeps &practice.

findings.title: Gamepad camera reset is labelled RS, but RS does nothing; it is Select/View, and LS toggles the survey with no label
findings.problem: The action bar's camera button shows a 'RS' pill (src/ui/screens.ts:55), and so does the pause-menu controls map (src/ui/screens.ts:169). Game.pollPad maps pad buttons as {8:'camera',10:'survey'} (src/game.ts:190). In the standard Gamepad mapping, 8 is Back/Select/View, 10 is the left-stick click and 11 (RS) is the right-stick click. RS is unbound. I tested with a fake standard-mapping pad injected through navigator.getGamepads. Pressing button 11 left the orbited, zoomed-in view unchanged (shot 71). Button 10 threw the camera into the survey (shot 72). Button 8 reset to the home view (shot 73). So a pad player who follows the HUD gets nothing, and a player who clicks the left stick by accident (common while sprinting) is thrown into the survey without knowing why. The survey has no pad label anywhere on the HUD or in the pause map.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:190, map 11:'camera' (RS click, which matches the label) and 8:'survey' (View/Back, the usual 'map' button), and drop 10. Alternatively keep the code and relabel the HUD to a View-button glyph. Add a survey row to the pause controls map (screens.ts:161-170) showing Tab plus the pad button, so the survey can be discovered on both inputs.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/meta-settings-errors/pad.mjs. Button 11 must restore the home framing (match shot 52), and the button labelled for survey must open the survey. Add a unit or e2e test that stubs navigator.getGamepads and asserts each labelled pill triggers its action.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:190 maps {8:'camera',10:'survey'}. In the W3C standard mapping, 8 is Back/View, 10 is the LS click and 11 is the RS click, so the 'RS' pill at screens.ts:55 and :169 labels a button that is unbound. Shot 72 (the reviewer's, which I viewed) shows the survey overview after button 10, with the HUD still showing the RS pill. I did not re-run the fake pad myself, but the code alone settles the claim. P1 is fair for pad players.

findings.title: At a bench, F, Space and Tab fall through to floor actions: F stands Pip up at QFN, Observatory and Spectrum, Space makes him jump, and Tab silently arms the survey
findings.room: qfn, observatory, spectrum (F); qfn (Space); all stations (Tab)
findings.problem:
The bench keydown branch (src/game.ts:166) gives a key to the station first. If station.key() returns false, the key falls through to the floor actions. In QFN the station keys are only C, L, R, V, Z (src/stations/qfn/station.ts:27); Observatory and Spectrum also have no KeyF. Measured at the QFN bench:
- **F:** action('cable') → interact(true) → `if(this.atBench){this.leaveBench();return;}` (src/game.ts:197), so F stands Pip up (atBench true → false). DR-22 makes F mean 'plug' everywhere; here it silently means 'stand up' at three benches, while Arcade and Garage use F for flip.
- **Space:** Pip jumps while seated (player y 0.77 → 1.59, with the jump sound), invisible behind the bench camera.
- **Tab:** toggles game.survey with no visible change at the bench (shot 63). When the player stands up, the camera flies to the survey framing (shot 64), which reads as a camera glitch.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:166, when atBench and the station didn't consume the key, `return` for KeyF, KeyQ, Space, Tab and KeyR instead of falling through (only E/Esc leave, and Escape-to-pause stays on the HUD button). Or set `this.survey=false` in leaveBench() and guard action('jump') and action('cable') with `!this.atBench`.
findings.verify: Extend tests/station-qfn.spec.ts: at the bench, press F, Space and Tab and expect atBench true and player.y within 0.05 of its seated value. Then Esc, and expect the camera at home zoom (not survey), checked by screenshot against meta-settings-errors-62.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced at the QFN bench. Space: player y went 0.769 → 1.594 while atBench stayed true. Tab then F: F left the bench (atBench false), and the camera landed in the whole-room survey framing (my shot 03), not the home view. The cause is in code: the bench branch at game.ts:164 only intercepts E/Esc and keys the station consumes, then falls through to the floor actions at :166, and interact() at :197 leaves the bench. Bench R is consumed by the QFN and Observatory stations, so adding KeyR to the guard is harmless.

findings.title: C at the QFN bench both runs CHECK and fires the floor camera reset
findings.problem: GameUI.key runs before Game's handler and calls game.action('camera') for KeyC whenever the screen is 'play' (src/ui/game-ui.ts:127). It doesn't check atBench. At the QFN bench, C is also the station's CHECK key (src/stations/qfn/station.ts:27, :101). One press therefore does both: the check runs (checks 1 → 2, measured), and action('camera') (src/game.ts:178) sets yaw=.14, pitch=0, zoom=homeZoom and survey=false. Outside ?manual the bench yaw then eases back from 0.14 rad to the bench's 0 rad over about 0.5 s (src/game.ts:372, `Math.min(1,dt*4)`). Every CHECK makes the table wobble 8°, which also moves the pointer-to-cell mapping the QFN spec has to wait out ('bench camera never settled', tests/station-qfn.spec.ts:74-78). It also throws away the player's chosen floor zoom when they stand up. (Under ?manual the yaw snaps back instantly, so the screenshot can't show it; the double action is shown by the counter and the code.)
findings.fix: In src/ui/game-ui.ts:127, add `&&!this.game.atBench` to the KeyC condition. Also make action('camera') a no-op while atBench (src/game.ts:178), so the pad camera button can't do it either.
findings.verify: In tests/station-qfn.spec.ts, after KeyC at the bench, press Esc and expect the floor zoom to equal the value set before sitting (expose zoom in snapshot()). Real-time run without ?manual: take two screenshots 0.1 s and 0.4 s after C and diff them. They must be identical.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in code; I did not reproduce the real-time wobble. GameUI.key (game-ui.ts:127) fires action('camera') for KeyC whenever the screen is 'play', with no atBench check. QFN maps KeyC to check (qfn/station.ts:27), and Game's bench branch passes C to the station as well, so one press does both. action('camera') (game.ts:178) sets yaw=.14 and zoom=homeZoom. The bench yaw then eases back with Math.min(1,dt*4) (game.ts:372), so a brief swing and the loss of the floor zoom both follow.

findings.title: The lens setting barely changes anything: Close, Standard and Wide differ by about 8–10% of view, and the bench ignores it
findings.problem:
The only camera setting is the pause tile 'View: Standard/Wide/Close' (src/ui/screens.ts:159; it cycles Standard → Wide → Close, src/game.ts:178). FOVS=[32,42,54] (src/render/lens.ts:5). lensScale (lens.ts:11) pulls the camera in to compensate, so the visible height at the focus point only scales by 1+(fov−30)/110: Close shows about 8% less than Standard and Wide about 10% more. Pip stays the same size on screen.
- **Floor:** with the view reset by C after each change, the three home views of the Playground (shots 52, 57, 58) look almost identical. None reaches the far wall, where the goal lamp is.
- **Bench:** the lens is exact on purpose (lens.ts:9-10), so the arcade bench is unchanged apart from the table corners touching the frame edge at Wide (shots 10, 11, 12).

There is no visible distortion and no cropped control at any setting, which is good, but the player gets no visible feedback from changing it. 'Close' also reads as 'camera closer', yet Pip isn't bigger. The default lens is 42°, while the rulebook's 'game camera FOV 30' convention and the lens.ts comment ('the 30° lens the zooms and bench views were tuned for') are stale.
findings.fix:
Make the setting mean something. Either:
- Turn it into a framing distance (multiply homeZoom by 0.8 / 1 / 1.25 and keep FOV 42). The labels 'Near / Standard / Far' then show visibly more room, and 'Far' can show the Playground goal.
- Or make the FOV choice not compensated (`lensScale` returns 1 for the walking camera), so Wide really shows about 30% more.

Also order the cycle Close → Standard → Wide. Update the rulebook's conventions table and the lens.ts comment to say the default is 42°.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/meta-settings-errors/settings.mjs. The three home shots should differ clearly (for example, the Playground lamp at (7,−6) is in frame at the far setting), and the arcade bench shots are unchanged.
findings.verify_reason: The math checks out. The visible height at the focus point is ∝ 2·dist·tan(fov/2) ∝ tan15°·(1+(fov−30)/110), which gives 1.018, 1.109 and 1.218 for 32°, 42° and 54°. Close is therefore −8% and Wide +10% against Standard, and the bench is exact (lens.ts:11). docs/PROGRESS.md:36 still says 'FOV 30' and the lens.ts comment references the 30° tuning, so that part is confirmed too. The lens.ts:2-4 doc comment shows this behaviour is intentional ('Pip stays big on screen'), so this is a clarity/value issue and P2 is right. I did not re-check the 'far wall / goal lamp not in frame' detail myself.
findings.fix_correction: One option makes the walking camera uncompensated. If chosen, check that Wide at the max zoom of 38 doesn't push into the survey's 44 framing and that the near-zoom Pip framing still holds. The safer option is the distance-multiplier variant.

findings.title: The camera-reset button and the lens tile share one 'photo camera' icon, so the reset reads as photo mode
findings.fix: Add a 'recenter' icon (a circular arrow around a small person, or a crosshair with a return arrow) to src/render/icons.ts. Use it for data-action="camera". Keep the camera glyph only for the lens/View tile, or give that tile an eye or aperture icon. In the pause map, split the row into 'right-drag = orbit', 'wheel = zoom', 'C = recenter'.
findings.verify: Retake the start shot and meta-settings-errors-20-pause-menu: the action bar shows the recenter glyph, and the pause map shows three separate camera rows.
findings.verify_reason: screens.ts:55, :159 and :169 all use icon('camera'). The pause shot shows the same compact-camera glyph on the 'View: Standard' tile and on the 'mouse + C → camera → RS' row, and the action bar uses it for reset. This is a subjective clarity call, but it is factually accurate. P2.

findings.title: Practice runs: the picker promises 'nothing is graded', but the card stamps a full grade, and the PRACTICE tag is hidden under the job card
findings.problem:
The practice flow works as designed. A full arcade solve with ?practice reached won=true, and localStorage circuit-crew:best:v1 stayed null, so nothing was recorded and Arcade Rush stays locked. Practice Restart keeps &practice. Station levels have no `next`, so no 'Next job' button can drop the flag. Three things don't match:
- **The picker text** says 'The whole job plays, nothing is graded or recorded' (src/hub/lobby.ts:113). The result card still shows the big 'A' stamp, per-axis grades (time A, damage B, cost A) and bonus stars (shot 41). Only a ~7 px-cap tag reads 'Practice · not recorded', squeezed in after the done-check (src/ui/game-ui.ts:214, ui.css:242; shot 44).
- **The in-run PRACTICE tag** (body[data-practice] .jobplate::after, src/ui/ui.css:243, bottom:-12px) is drawn under the objective card, so only the top half of 'PRACTICE' shows (shots 40 and 43). During play the player can't tell they're in practice.
- **The spelling** is mixed: 'Practise any station' on the picker, 'Practice' on the tag and card (DR-50, already listed for L3; still open).
findings.fix:
Change the picker copy to 'Practice any station. Your grade isn't saved.' Then do the following:
- **Result card:** in practice, move the tag into the stamp zone as a 14 px+ 'PRACTICE' ribbon across the medal (or grey the medal), and put it before the check.
- **In-run tag:** in ui.css:243, place it on the jobplate's right side (`left:auto;right:-8px;top:-8px;bottom:auto`) or give it a z-index above .objective, so it isn't covered.
- **Spelling:** use 'practice' everywhere.
findings.verify: Retake meta-settings-errors-40 and -41 with practice.mjs. The PRACTICE tag is fully visible above the job card, and the result card shows a legible practice ribbon. grep 'Practise' in src/ returns nothing.
findings.verify_reason: Viewed crop 43: the in-run PRACTICE tag is half covered by the objective card (ui.css:243, bottom:-12px). Result shot 41 shows the full A medal, the per-axis grades and stars, with only a small 'Practice · not recorded' pill (12px font, ui.css:242), which contradicts lobby.ts:113 'nothing is graded'. The 'Practise' spelling is at lobby.ts:113. The '~7 px cap' figure is a little low (a 12 px font has about an 8–9 px cap), but the pill is small either way.

findings.title: The Lunch fail card holds for 1.2 s with no input, then needs Enter or a click; retrying itself takes about 0.6 s
findings.problem:
Measured with flows.mjs (DR-20):
- **Fail to card:** the fridge spoil fires, the room alarms and groans, and the card appears 1.2 s later (setTimeout 1200, src/lunch-runtime.ts:286).
- **During the hold:** g.won=true, so no game input is accepted.
- **Retry:** pressing Enter on the card reloaded the page, autostarted and accepted input (running, screen 'play') in 565 ms.

The total is about 1.8 s, which is within DR-20's 3 s. But the only advertised key (R) is dead (see the R finding), and keyboard focus only lands on Retry if the last input was a key. A mouse player must click. Bench failures compare well: an Arcade fuse trip and a QFN send-back both accept the next input immediately (act slot/pick/check returned ok at once while the fuse was still cooling, 2.35 s left). So DR-20 passes for the stations, and Lunch's only gap is the key. Logged as P2 because it is mostly a timing confirmation.
findings.fix: Besides the R fix, let R, Enter and E retry already during the 1.2 s hold: flag a pending retry and fire it when the card mounts, so an impatient player isn't ignored. Always focus the Retry button when the card mounts (drop the `this.keyboard` condition at game-ui.ts:240 for the fail screen only).
findings.verify: In flows.mjs, press R 0.5 s after job.failed and expect screen 'play' within 2.5 s of the failure.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in code: setTimeout 1200 before the card (lunch-runtime.ts:286), won=true during the hold, and the card is focused only when this.keyboard (game-ui.ts:240). I did not re-measure the 565 ms reload or the station timings. This mostly duplicates finding 0. Its one new suggestion, accepting input during the hold, partly conflicts with finding 0's own advice to keep the hold so the payoff isn't skipped.
findings.fix_correction: Buffer an R/Enter press made during the 1.2 s hold and fire it only once the card has mounted and been visible for at least about 0.3 s, so the failure beat still reads. Don't skip the hold outright. Always focusing Retry on mount is fine.

findings.title: The muted state of the Sound tile is shown only by a swapped glyph and a faint tint; the label still reads 'Sound'
findings.problem: Mute works and persists. Clicking the pause tile set localStorage circuit-crew-muted='1' (src/render/audio.ts:18). The setting survived a page reload (aria-pressed true, #i-mute icon) and a trip to the lobby through 'Jobs'. The AudioContext master gain starts at 0 when muted (audio.ts:24). Observatory's own sound also checks a.muted (src/stations/observatory/station.ts:333). The only problem is legibility. The tile keeps the text 'Sound' in both states. syncSound (src/ui/game-ui.ts:142-143) only swaps the icon href and removes the green 'on' tint. In the 4-tile row, the difference is a small speaker glyph with or without an X. The lens tile next to it, by contrast, says 'View: Standard'.
findings.fix: In syncSound, also set the label: `b.querySelector('span').textContent=muted?'Muted':'Sound'`. Give the muted tile a distinct style, such as a red-tinted background like `.tile.off`.
findings.verify: Retake meta-settings-errors-50: the muted tile reads 'Muted' with a distinct colour, and the state survives a reload.
findings.verify_reason: Shot 50 shows the muted tile still labelled 'Sound', with only the speaker-X glyph and the lost tint as cues. syncSound (game-ui.ts:142-143) swaps only aria-pressed, the 'on' class and the icon href, never the label. The persistence key is audio.ts:18. Purely cosmetic, so P2.
findings.fix_correction: The tile has two spans only when the label span is the first span. Use `b.querySelector('span:not(.key)')` or add a data-p="sound" span (like data-p="lens"), so the selector doesn't hit the wrong element.

notes.playability:
DR-80: every level id passes start, survey (Tab in and out) and a 20 s scripted walk with zero console or page errors. This was run with errors.mjs and g.close() for each level; output verbatim:
- lobby errors []
- playground []
- meeting []
- lunch []
- arcade []
- arcade-rush []
- garage []
- qfn []
- observatory []
- spectrum []

The walk was W, D, S, A with sprint, plus E, Q, Space and F presses. These scripts also closed with errors []:
- the Playground win;
- a full Arcade practice solve;
- the Lunch spoil fail and retry;
- the QFN send-back, CHECK, Tab and stand-up;
- the Arcade fuse trip;
- the fake-gamepad run;
- the lens cycling in Meeting and at the Arcade bench.

g.audit(.02) after 0.5 s of settling returned [] for meeting, arcade and qfn. The non-zero counts in errors.mjs (meeting 1, arcade 1, arcade-rush 1, qfn 2) were taken after the walk had knocked props together, not at start.

Start-of-level draw calls, which count every render pass (src/game.ts:450):

| Level | Draw calls at start |
|---|---|
| lobby | 592 |
| playground | 782 |
| meeting | 1315 |
| lunch | 1309 |
| arcade | 1497 |
| garage | 1156 |
| qfn | 1201 |
| observatory | 1094 |
| spectrum | 1133 |

Fps in ?manual is not meaningful.

DR-20: bench failures are cheap. Inputs are accepted at once during an Arcade fuse trip and right after a QFN send-back. Lunch is about 1.8 s from failure to playable through Enter. R is broken on both end cards.

The main control bugs are at the meta layer:
- R is dead on the result and fail cards.
- The pad camera button is labelled RS but bound to Select, and LS opens an unlabelled survey.
- At benches, F, Space and Tab fall through to floor actions.
- C at the QFN bench doubles as a camera reset.

The C reset itself works well: it returns to the exact home view from any orbit, zoom or the survey.
notes.clarity:
The settings surface is small: a Sound tile and a 'View' lens tile in pause, the C button on the action bar, and a sound button on the title screen. Both settings persist in localStorage (circuit-crew-muted, circuit-crew-fov) across a reload and a lobby round-trip.

The lens setting is too subtle to notice (about 8–10%), and 'Close' doesn't bring the camera closer. One photo-camera glyph stands for three different things: reset, lens, and orbit/zoom in the controls map.

The Sound tile never changes its label. Practice mode is hard to notice during a run, because the PRACTICE tag sits under the job card. On the result card the tag is about 7 px, while a full A-stamp grade sits next to it, after the picker promised 'nothing is graded'.

At a bench, Esc stands Pip up rather than pausing (as DR-22 intends), so the lens and mute settings can only be reached there through the HUD pause button.
notes.models: Not in scope for this gap-fill. No model findings beyond what the room reviewers filed. At Close zoom with the Wide lens, the objective marker becomes a large flat cone; that is already filed under the marker findings.
notes.fun: Meta paths don't affect fun directly. The win push-in and the result card's count-up and confetti still land. The fail card's iconography (spoiled bowl, thermometer, the three-step progress chain) is clear without text. The friction is all in the retry key.
notes.teaching: No teaching content in the meta screens. The fail card shows how far the tray got (oven, belt, lift) with icons only, which fits DR-40. The cause sentence lives in the world beat beforehand: groans and puffs at the fridge, per DR-28. Practice mode keeps the full grading, which is arguably good for learning, but the copy should say 'not saved' rather than 'not graded'.

rechecked: L6 (Tab and R act only during play, 65a7344): Tab is correctly blocked on menus. R now also does nothing on the result and fail cards, which still show an R keycap. Treat it as a REGRESSION side effect, filed under DR-19 and DR-20.
L5 (no Jobs-board reopen on reload): not regressed. The 'Jobs' button lands in the lobby in play mode (url ?level=lobby, screen play).
LR4 (in-world fail beat before the card): still FIXED. A 1.2 s hold with groans and puffs comes before the spoil card.
A11 (stale toast hidden on sit): the QFN check toast stays up for its max(4 s, len·0.06 s) timer after standing up (shot 64). Minor, not a regression of A11.
LR15 (Lunch about 175 draw calls): the snapshot now reads 1309 at start. That is not comparable, because the counter now sums every pass (src/game.ts:450). Flagged for the perf owner, not filed.
DR-80: all 10 level ids report no errors (start, survey, 20 s walk, plus several solve and fail scripts).
